Read the following and identify the single biggest risk, explaining why it outranks the others. Our company runs a payments platform processing about 40,000 transactions a day. The core service is a five-year-old Java application maintained by three engineers, two of whom joined in the last six months. The original author left last year without writing documentation. We have 62% test coverage, though most of it is on utility code rather than the payment flows. Deployments happen manually on Thursday evenings and take about ninety minutes, with a rollback procedure that has been used twice and failed once. Database backups run nightly and have never been restored in a drill. A new regulatory requirement will force changes to the settlement logic within four months. Our largest customer, representing 30% of volume, has a contract renewal in five months and has recently complained about two outages.

Summarise the decision the team should make, given this context. A SaaS company with 18 employees has been running on a single cloud provider since founding. Their monthly bill has risen from 4,000 to 31,000 dollars over two years, with 60% attributable to a managed database and 25% to egress charges from serving media files. Growth is steady at 8% monthly. A board member has suggested moving to a cheaper provider, estimating 40% savings. The engineering lead estimates migration would take two engineers four months, during which the product roadmap would stall. The company has 14 months of runway and is planning to raise in nine months. Two competitors have recently shipped features the team has not matched.

Based on the following, explain whether the hiring plan is sound and what you would change. A 25-person engineering organisation plans to hire 15 more engineers over the next nine months. Currently there are three teams, each with a tech lead who also writes code full time. Onboarding takes roughly six weeks before a new hire ships independently, and the internal documentation was last updated eleven months ago. Two of the three tech leads have expressed interest in management but have never managed anyone. The interview process involves five rounds and the offer acceptance rate is 45%. Attrition over the past year was 20%, concentrated among engineers with less than eighteen months tenure.

Identify the contradictions in the following requirements and explain which ones cannot all be satisfied simultaneously. The new internal tool must be accessible to all employees without login friction, but must also maintain a full per-user audit trail for compliance. It should work offline in warehouses with no connectivity, while always displaying real-time inventory counts. It must be delivered in eight weeks using the existing two-person team, who are also responsible for maintaining the current tool. The design should be finalised before development starts, but stakeholders want to see working software within three weeks to give feedback.

An open-source alternative exists but lacks two features used in four of the twelve lab exercises. Faculty are split: three prefer switching, two strongly oppose, one is neutral. Rewriting the affected exercises would take roughly 60 hours of faculty time. The department budget was cut 15% this year. Students have occasionally complained that the licensed software is unavailable off-campus.
